extracted.intended_audience: researchers and community members who want to write, request, or manage preprint reviews on PREreview.org
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and platform-level rules for creating, publishing, and requesting open preprint reviews on the PREreview.org site (including account/identity, review formats, request workflows, and community resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID login requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You’ll need an ORCID iD to login to PREreview.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PREreview requires signing in with an ORCID iD to publish reviews. Your PREreview account ties to that ORCID identity and enables the platform's publication features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account display name options (pseudonym vs public name)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your PREreview account will give you access to two names with which you can publish your PREreviews. One is your PREreview pseudonym which is a preassigned and uneditable combination of an animal and a color (e.g. Yellow Penguin). The other is the name corresponding to your ORCID iD (here referred to as your public name). If you choose to publish a review with your pseudonym, your public name will remain hidden unless you disclose your pseudonym to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may publish under either the auto-generated PREreview pseudonym or your ORCID-linked public name; the pseudonym is uneditable. This controls public attribution; PREreview staff retain internal access to identities in case of Code of Conduct violations but will not share pseudonyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and staff access policy for identity
rubrics_metrics.description: PREreview staff can access all users' identity via our database should a violation of Code of Conduct be reported. We will never share your PREreview pseudonym with anyone, and it is not something we access unless there is a need to communicate with a preprint review author or to temporarily or permanently block a user account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff access is reserved for handling misconduct reports and account actions. Users' pseudonyms are not disclosed to others by PREreview.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to start/publish a PREreview (workflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Click the big red “Review a preprint” button in the middle of the page to start authoring your own PREreview! Once you click the button, you’ll be guided through a helpful workflow that will help you complete your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the platform's guided workflow to create and publish a review. The workflow presents choices (Structured, Templated, Freeform) and steps to completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of review format: Structured, Templated, or Freeform
rubrics_metrics.description: You’ll also have the option to start a Structured PREreview (with prompts from us), a Templated PREreview (with a basic, suggested framework from us), or a Freeform PREreview (with just a text box you can type in or copy/paste a PREreview you drafted elsewhere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured PREreviews include platform prompts; Templated offers a suggested framework; Freeform is an open text box. The site allows previewing Structured PREreview prompts before beginning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preview Structured PREreview prompts before beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: If you would like to review our Structured PREreview prompts before beginning a Structured PREreview, you can find them here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can inspect the structured prompts in advance to decide whether to use that format for their review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting a review on PREreview.org (DOI required)
rubrics_metrics.description: To request a review on PREreview.org, click on the 'Request a review' link next to the 'Review a preprint' button. You will need the DOI of the preprint you would like to request for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting a review through the site requires the preprint DOI; the request will show on the PREreview homepage and Recent review requests page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported preprint servers for review requests
rubrics_metrics.description: You can currently request a review of any preprint on bioRxiv, SciELO Preprints, arXiv, EcoEvoRxiv, EdArXiv, medRxiv, OSF, PsyArXiv, and SocArXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PREreview will add support for more servers over time; users can email help@prereview.org to request support for additional servers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting a review via Slack (#request-a-review) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: To request a review on our Slack community, please create an account there and then visit the #request-a-review channel. You can type in any request for review you'd like to share on that channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requesting on Slack, include the DOI of the preprint and some information about it to help potential reviewers know if they are a good match. Slack requests should appear on PREreview.org as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting a review as a preprint author on integrated servers
rubrics_metrics.description: To request a review as a preprint author on bioRxiv, SciELO preprints, or Preprints.org, click on the option to request a review when you publish your preprint on either server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author-initiated requests made on those preprint servers will surface on PREreview.org and in the Slack community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtering Recent PREreviews and review requests by language and field
rubrics_metrics.description: On our Recent PREreviews page, you can filter review search results by language and research field. On our Recent review requests page, you can also filter request search results by language and field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the language and field filters to find reviews or requests relevant to your expertise or language preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainings and Live Review offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Visit the Trainings page to learn more about our Open Reviewers training programs, how much our workshops cost for institutions, and how to participate as an individual researcher. We also facilitate Live Review calls for groups who want to get better at collaborative review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PREreview provides both recorded/structured trainings and live facilitated workshops for individuals and institutions; pricing and participation details are on the Trainings and Live Reviews pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: PREreview Clubs (collaborative review groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: PREreview Clubs are collaborative preprint reviewing groups around a shared affiliation, affinity, interest, location, or any other common cause. Find out how to start your own PREreview Club on the Clubs page!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs are intended for groups to organize regular collaborative preprint reviewing; the site provides guidance on starting and running a Club.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footer community and governance resources (Code of Conduct, EDI, newsletter, Slack, GitHub)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our footer has all kinds of helpful meta-information about PREreview that you might want to review as a community member, funder, or potential user. For example, you can learn more about our Code of Conduct and EDI Statement. You can also find links to our newsletter, Slack community, and GitHub repository (as well as other social media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The footer links provide community governance information (Code of Conduct, equity/diversity/inclusion statement) and channels for updates and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zenodo API for querying review data and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Because PREreview stores its reviews and their metadata on Zenodo, the best way to make queries about that data associated with PREreview is through the Zenodo API (linked to from our Footer). You can find the Zenodo API documentation here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For data-related questions or custom queries, use the Zenodo API or contact help@prereview.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sandbox environment for testing workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: On our “sandbox” at https://sandbox.prereview.org, you can explore the site and try out different features like starting a review or requesting a review without actually adding anything to your review or request history on PREreview.org, itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the sandbox to test features and workflows safely; nothing is published there and actions do not affect your real account history.
